key_insight: Pretrained MobileNet with differential attention achieved the best slide-level discrimination of high- versus low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, while adding spatial attention showed no detectable benefit.
clinical_relevance: This grading study—not drug discovery—could inform future pathology decision-support tools, but does not establish clinical readiness.
method: Compared CNN attention variants, pretrained MobileNet, and a Phikon foundation-model benchmark.
Used stain normalisation, slide-level pooling, and five-fold slide-grouped cross-validation.
Evaluated three training seeds with within-fold threshold selection and multiplicity-adjusted statistical comparisons.
evidence_signal: On 259 slides (217 high-grade, 42 low-grade), pretrained MobileNet achieved AUC 0.862 ± 0.005 and MCC 0.460, significantly outperforming the no-attention baseline.
watch_item: The small, imbalanced single-cohort evaluation and colour-only AUC of 0.66 warrant external validation for stain-related confounding and generalisability.
paper_title: Which Attention Helps? A Slide-Level Ablation of Attention-Augmented CNNs for Serous Ovarian Carcinoma Grading
